theme: The Binance hack knocks bitcoin below $77K as Strategy reports a $20.9B bitcoin gain, Big Tech cash flow and AI debt take center stage, and SpaceX's profits fuel merger talk with Tesla.

items.title: Bitcoin held on exchanges as a % of supply
items.picked: Binance disclosed a security breach affecting about $6.3B in assets, the largest crypto theft on record, and bitcoin fell below $77,000 overnight before recovering toward $78,000. Binance says it has frozen about $3B, will cover all losses, and has suspended deposits and withdrawals.
items.matters: Hacks like this are the classic argument for keeping coins off exchanges, and the share of supply sitting on exchanges shows how much bitcoin is exposed to that kind of risk.
items.know: The tab has 13.37% of bitcoin supply on exchanges as of Oct 25 2026, close to 13.35% at the end of September and up from a 12.88% low in Apr 2026, which the chart title calls the lowest since May 2018. The Oct 25 point is a flash value and predates the hack, and the image is the Oct 19 export, so it ends with September. Coin Metrics only counts the exchange wallets it has tagged, and that coverage has changed over time.

items.title: Strategy's bitcoin gain or loss by quarter
items.picked: Strategy reported Q3 results after the close Thursday, with a $20.91B gain on its bitcoin and diluted EPS of $44.75, well above the $13.86 estimate per Investing.com. Bitcoin has since dropped below $77,000 on the Binance hack.
items.matters: Strategy's earnings swing with the bitcoin price, so this chart shows how much of its reported profit and loss is just mark-to-market on its holdings.
items.know: The tab shows a $20.91B Q3 2026 gain after three losing quarters: -$17.44B in Q4 2025, -$14.455B in Q1 2026 and -$8.315B in Q2 2026. Q3 is still labeled an estimate from the Oct 5 8-K, but Thursday's results reported the same $20.91B. These are unrealized fair-value moves, and Q4 starts with bitcoin well below the $81,200 Strategy used on Oct 23.

items.title: Amazon: operating cash flow, capex and free cash flow per quarter
items.picked: Amazon fell about 7% premarket after missing on revenue and earnings and reporting negative free cash flow again, per CNBC. It kept its 2026 capex forecast at $220B and signaled more spending next year.
items.matters: Amazon is the biggest capex spender in the tab, and its cash flow shows how much of the AI buildout is being paid for out of operations.
items.know: In the Jun 2026 quarter the tab has operating cash flow of $45.39B, capex of $54.21B and free cash flow of -$8.82B, after -$18.17B in Mar 2026; a year earlier it was +$0.33B. The tab ends with the Jun quarter, so Thursday's Sep-quarter numbers aren't in it yet. Amazon's own free cash flow figure is trailing 12 months, so it won't match these single-quarter numbers.

items.title: Big Tech 4: quarterly capex vs free cash flow
items.picked: After this week's results from Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon, Nasdaq-100 futures fell about 2.4% on AI spending worries. A Swissquote analyst told Reuters the four spent more than $200B on capex in the third quarter alone.
items.matters: When capex eats nearly all of operating cash flow, there's little left for buybacks, dividends or paying down debt, which is why the market is now focused on returns from AI spending.
items.know: In the Jun 2026 quarter the four companies' capex was $165.05B against $171.76B of operating cash flow, or 96.09%, leaving $6.71B of free cash flow. A year earlier capex was $88.25B and free cash flow $40.22B. The tab ends with the Jun quarter, so the Sep quarter isn't in it yet.

items.title: Borrowing for AI: total debt by company, fiscal year ends vs latest quarter
items.picked: Microsoft raised $25B in a debt sale even as it beat on cash flow, and Reuters says several companies have tapped the bond market to fund AI spending. House Democrats also introduced a resolution opposing taxpayer bailouts for AI firms.
items.matters: Debt is the newer way Big Tech funds the AI buildout, and higher borrowing costs could make that spending harder to justify.
items.know: As of Jun 2026 the tab has Amazon at $133B of debt, Oracle $129.5B, Alphabet $101.1B, Meta $83.7B, Microsoft $40.3B and CoreWeave $35.6B. Alphabet's debt is up from $49.1B and Meta's from $58.7B at their FY 2025 year ends. The latest column is Jun 2026, so Microsoft's new $25B bond and other Sep-quarter borrowing aren't in it, and fiscal years end in different months for each company.

items.title: Reported revenue run-rates: OpenAI vs Anthropic
items.picked: Anthropic filed for its US IPO this week, and Bloomberg reports it was SpaceX's largest customer, providing more than a third of SpaceX's Q3 revenue through compute deals.
items.matters: Anthropic's revenue growth is what backs its valuation and its huge compute commitments, which now show up in SpaceX's and the neoclouds' results.
items.know: The tab's latest points, both from Sep 2026, are a $100B annualized run-rate for Anthropic and $70B for OpenAI. Anthropic was at $1B in Dec 2024 and $9B in Dec 2025. These are run-rates from company statements and media reports on irregular dates, not reported annual revenue, and the chart uses a log scale.

items.title: Data center capacity by country: operational today plus pipeline (GW)
items.picked: Epoch AI's post that 72% of the world's AI compute since 2022 has ended up in the US, and 78% of new compute in the first half of 2026, is trending on X. This chart shows the same US lead in data center power.
items.matters: Compute needs powered data center space, so the capacity pipeline shows where AI chips can actually be installed in the next few years.
items.know: The tab has the US at 31.97 GW operational and 70.63 GW in the pipeline (102.6 GW total), against China at 5.49 GW and 2.66 GW. Of the 15 countries listed, the US has about 60% of operational capacity and 71% of the pipeline. The data is a Cushman & Wakefield snapshot published Apr 15 2026, measures power capacity rather than compute, and this image was drawn from the sheet because there's no Drive export for this tab.

items.title: SpaceX operating income by segment: Space, Starlink and AI
items.picked: A post on X says SpaceX made 3.9x Tesla's Q3 operating profit, $2.79B against $718M, on about half the revenue. SpaceX's Q3 filing puts Starlink at $2.367B of that and its AI segment at $431M.
items.matters: Starlink is the profit engine that pays for SpaceX's rocket and AI spending, and the AI segment's swing to a profit in Q3 is new.
items.know: For the four quarters to Sep 30 2026 the tab has Starlink operating income of $6.488B, against losses of $5.468B in AI and $1.688B in Space, a combined -$0.67B. That compares with $4.423B, -$6.355B and -$0.657B for 2025. The Drive export still showed the older TTM to Jun 2026, so this image was redrawn from the sheet.

items.title: SpaceX vs Tesla market value since the IPO
items.picked: Musk called a Tesla-SpaceX merger 'a good idea' and both companies have formed independent board committees to look at it. Prediction markets on X put the odds at about 65% by May 2027.
items.matters: The relative value of the two companies would set the terms of any merger, so the ratio is the number both sets of shareholders will watch.
items.know: On Oct 20 the tab has SpaceX at $1,948B and Tesla at $1,476B, a ratio of 1.32x. The ratio peaked at 1.743x on Jun 16, the IPO week, and fell to 1.029x on Jul 22. The data ends Oct 20, so it misses SPCX's slide toward $140 after last week's share unlock.

items.title: Tech leadership: Nasdaq Composite ÷ S&P 500
items.picked: Nasdaq-100 futures fell about 2.4% this morning while S&P 500 futures fell about 1%, after Amazon and Intel results added to AI spending worries. The Nasdaq is on track to break a two-month winning streak in October.
items.matters: The ratio shows whether tech is leading or lagging the broader market, and a falling ratio means money is rotating out of tech.
items.know: The tab's latest weekly point in October is 3.4495 (Nasdaq 26,713.03, S&P 500 7,744.06), down from 3.5209 earlier in the month. The high in the data is 3.5822 in Feb 2021, and it reached 3.5584 in May 2026. The weekly rows are only labeled by month and end before this week's selloff.
